Known Data Issues

Source: vignettes/known-data-issues.Rmd
known-data-issues.Rmd

This page lists known limitations of the data in EJAM v4.2024.0, which uses the 2020-2024 American Community Survey (ACS). Each one affects a small number of places. They are documented here so that results for those places can be interpreted correctly, and most are planned for correction in a later release.

To report a problem not listed here, open an issue in the EJAM repository.

Brentwood and Wyandanch, New York: no ACS 2020-2024 data

The Census Bureau withheld the ACS 2019-2023 and 2020-2024 estimates for the Brentwood and Wyandanch census-designated places in Suffolk County, New York (Census errata note 148).

  • EJAM therefore has no data for the 39 blockgroups (in 14 tracts) that make up those places, home to about 75,000 residents.
  • An analysis that includes any part of those places counts no residents there, so it undercounts residents and shows no indicator values for those areas.
  • Results for Suffolk County as a whole also exclude these residents, so they are lower than the Census Bureau’s own county total.

EJAM v3.2022.3 (ACS 2018-2022) does include these blockgroups, but it is not an unaffected alternative. The same Census note explains that the suppression results from a data collection error, and it advises caution when using the 2016-2020, 2017-2021 and 2018-2022 estimates for these places. Those older values should not be used to fill in the missing v4.2024.0 values.

Connecticut

Starting with 2022 geography, the Census Bureau uses Connecticut’s nine planning regions as county equivalents, in place of its eight former counties. EJAM uses the planning regions. Two small issues remain from that change (EJAM issue 19):

  • About 300 residents are not counted. Nineteen blockgroup codes in EJAM’s Census 2020 block crosswalk use outdated codes. The 21 Census blocks assigned to them, with about 300 residents in total, are left out of analyses. Each of those blocks lies within a blockgroup that EJAM does have, so the effect is a slight undercount near those locations.
  • Five coastal water blockgroups have no ozone or PM2.5 values. These blockgroups cover water only and have no residents, so no analysis results change.

Places with no county code

About 370 entries in EJAM’s built-in table of cities, towns and other places (censusplaces) have no county FIPS code. Most are places in Connecticut, plus a few in Alaska, South Dakota, Virginia and Louisiana, whose counties were renamed or reorganized after the source list was published. Features that rely on a place’s county code may not work for those places.

State averages are blockgroup averages

A report’s “state average” for an indicator is the average across the state’s blockgroups, as in EJSCREEN. It is not the average for the state’s residents, which would weight each blockgroup by its population. As a result, an analysis of an entire state can show a ratio to the state average that is slightly different from 1 (EJAM issue 66).

Small percentile differences from the EJSCREEN map layers

For 98 blockgroups, the percentile EJAM reports for drinking water non-compliance (77 blockgroups) or ozone (21 blockgroups) differs from the percentile in the EJSCREEN map layers by 1 to 3 percentile points. The indicator values themselves are identical. The difference comes from how tied values are ranked when they differ only by floating-point rounding. Percentiles of the EJ indexes are not affected.

Very large analyses in the web app

Analyses of many thousands of sites, especially with larger radii, use a lot of memory on the server. In the web app they can be slow, and requests that are too large stop with an explanation instead of running (EJAM issue 504). For very large analyses, use the EJAM R package on a computer with enough memory.

Island Areas

The ACS does not cover American Samoa, Guam, the Northern Mariana Islands or the U.S. Virgin Islands, so EJAM has limited residential population information for them. See Island Areas.
